notes.4iii: This proved to be an easy question, though accuracy presented many candidates with a problem. Many answers were given as “8 cm² ” instead of “7.96 cm² ”. As in part (ii), the only method error was to assume that the radius was 10 cm. Answers: (i) Proof. (ii) 20.4 cm. (iii) 7.95 or 7.96 cm².
notes.5i: This presented most candidates with problems. The squaring of the brackets was poor with such errors as (−3cosθ)² = −9cos²θ or 3cos²θ being very common. Consequently it was relatively rare for candidates to finish with an expression of the form kcos²θ + ksin²θ. Many candidates obtained the answer 10sin²θ + 10cos²θ but failed to realise that this had a constant value of 10.
notes.5iii: This was well answered and the majority of candidates obtained the equation tanθ = − 7 and proceeded to give correct values in the second and fourth quadrants. Even when poor algebra led to a value for tanθ other than −7, the method mark and follow-through mark for the second angle were usually obtained. Answers: (i) 10. (ii) 98.1º, 278.1º.
notes.6: This question was extremely well answered and it was particularly pleasing that the concept of unit vector was much better understood than in previous years.
notes.6i: Of the three parts, this caused most difficulty with many candidates failing to realise that if two vectors are parallel, all of the three components must be in same ratio, leading directly to p = −6 and q = 6.
notes.6iii: Most candidates realised that ABwas obtained from b – a and obtained a correct expression. The vast majority of candidates also realised the need to divide ABby its modulus. Only a small 9709 Mathematics June 2013 proportion of candidates incorrectly used ABas a + b. It was of concern that several candidates 2+3+6 left the answer as a number rather than a vector (usually ). Answers: (i) p = −6, q = 6. (ii) −1.5. (iii) (2i + 3j + 6k).
notes.7: This presented the majority of candidates with problems. Many candidates automatically associated the word “reflection” with the inverse of a function and attempted to find the equation of a line which was the mirror image of the original line in the line y = x. Very little progress was subsequently made. Those giving the situation a little more thought realised that R lay on the perpendicular from (−1, 3) to the original line. These candidates had little difficulty in finding the equation of this perpendicular which was then solved simultaneously with the original equation to obtain the point (3, 9). A common error was to assume that this was the point R, but most of these candidates proceeded to find the coordinates of R by vector steps or use of the midpoint. Answer: (7, 15)

notes.10a: This produced many correct answers with candidates confidently setting the sum of the first four terms to 57, finding the value of the common difference and using this to find the value of n.
notes.10b: Although many candidates obtained one correct value of k, the second was usually missing when the solution of r²=4 was given as r = 2, instead of r = ±2. Surprisingly many candidates failed to cancel a in the equation ar² = 4a and never obtained a numerical value for r whilst others obtained r = ±2 and automatically gave the answers as ±63. Answers: (a) n = 25. (b) k = 63 or −21.
notes.11i: This part of the question was very well answered. The differentiation was generally accurate, with only a small number of candidates omitting the “×4” from the differential. Finding the gradient of both the tangent and the normal and hence the equation of the normal presented few problems. The only common error was to give the equation of the tangent rather than the normal.
notes.11iii: Most candidates realised the need to integrate a composite function and the standard of integration was good. Coming to a final answer presented more difficulty, and although the lower limit of −¼ was used by most candidates, it was common to see an upper limit of 2, rather than 0. It was also rare to see a correct answer for the area of the triangle BOC. Some weaker candidates also assumed that the shaded region was a sector of a circle. Answers: (i) 2y + x = 2. (ii) 1 .

notes.general_comments:
The paper gave all candidates the chance to show what they had learnt. It was particularly pleasing that the
concept of “unit vector”, which in previous years had presented so many problems, was fully understand by
the majority of candidates. Although the standard of presentation was generally good, there were many
scripts which were difficult to mark because of poor presentation and lack of working. Again candidates (and
Centres) need to realise that the splitting of a page into columns, whilst being acceptable in the classroom, is
an unacceptable practice in an examination. It is a practice which makes marking extremely difficult.
